fit: tea exposure and separate olfactory phenotype in a GBA1 family survey
assessment: The study compared tea exposure against Parkinson status and hyposmia by group in 59 nonmanifesting GBA1 carriers, 62 controls and 107 GBA1-Parkinson cases. Available author text gives no tea-by-hyposmia comparison or brewed preparation. Full tables remain open.

fit: tea and hyposmia tested as separate cfDNA methylation correlates
assessment: The abstract describes 20 Parkinson participants and nine controls. It reports separate phenotypic associations with methylation without a tea-to-hyposmia estimate or beverage preparation. Possible participant overlap with a different clinical report is unverified.

fit: corn-oil comparator and MADRS depression in the OmegAD cohort
assessment: Six-month corn-oil MADRS means 1.9 to 1.6, versus 1.8 to 1.5 for omega-3, between-arm p=.49. APOE epsilon-4 noncarriers favored omega-3 in a small subgroup. This Alzheimer's study lacks a separate oil-free group, refined oil grade, or Parkinson-specific outcome.

fit: oral corn-oil comparator and broad NPI nighttime behavior item in Alzheimer disease
assessment: Six-month nighttime behavior p=.69. Corn-oil means 4.9 to 3.7 among item-positive subsets of 33 and 19. Changing denominators and a broad nighttime item leave an insomnia outcome unresolved. No refining grade or no-oil arm.

fit: registered mixed topical lotion and global sleep quality outside Parkinson disease
assessment: Single-arm topical lotion includes Cymbopogon flexuosus oil and citral, plus melatonin and other components. The registry gives 35 actual participants and no posted results. SQS and Fitbit do not measure enacted dreams or REM without atonia. No brewed tea.
